fields.spec_version: JEDEC JESD209-5 — Low Power Double Data Rate 5 (LPDDR5) SDRAM Standard (published 19 February 2019), with addenda JESD209-5B (LPDDR5/5X, 28 July 2021) and JESD209-5X (LPDDR5X).

spec_lineage_lpddr.summary: Original low-power DDR; 1.8 V (vs 2.5 V SDRAM); temperature-compensated / partial-array self-refresh; deep power-down; mobile-optimized.
1.2 V; 2n (S2) or 4n (S4) prefetch, plus non-volatile (N) option; 10-bit double-data-rate CA bus; up to LPDDR2-1066.
1600 MT/s; write-leveling, command/address training, optional on-die termination; 10-bit DDR CA bus; 8n prefetch.

Two independent 16-bit channels per die; 6-bit SDR-named CA bus (CS active-high; two-cycle commands); doubled prefetch (16n); self-refresh via dedicated commands (no CKE); DBI; up to 3200 MT/s. LPDDR4X reduces Vddq to 0.6 V.

WCK / RDQS on-demand clocking with quarter-speed CK; 7-bit DDR CA bus; 16 banks in 4 bank groups; 16n prefetch (not doubled); VDDQ 0.5 V; link ECC; DVFS/DVFSC; deep sleep; Data-Copy / Write-X; CKE eliminated; up to 6400 Mbps.
Speed extension up to 8533 Mbit/s; tx/rx equalization for SI; Adaptive Refresh Management for reliability.
Successor (JESD-future); CA bus narrowed further; data bus width 12 bits per channel; higher speeds. Out of scope of JESD209-5.

previous_versions_of_this_spec.summary: LPDDR5/5X update: speed up to 8533 Mbit/s; tx/rx equalization; Adaptive Refresh Management.
LPDDR5X branded extension; later devices reach 8533+ Mbit/s on 14/12 nm-class processes (LPDDR5X-8533 / LPDDR5T-9600 / LPDDR5X-10700).

key_changes_vs_lpddr4.change: New clocking architecture: quarter-speed CK + on-demand full-speed WCK + DRAM-driven RDQS
key_changes_vs_lpddr4.impact: WCK/RDQS enabled only when needed → major IO power saving vs a continuous data clock; requires WCK2CK synchronization before every high-speed transfer.

key_changes_vs_lpddr4.change: CA bus widened to 7 bits, transferred at double data rate
key_changes_vs_lpddr4.impact: Commands arrive at the same cadence as LPDDR4 despite the quarter-speed CK; a command spans two CA transfers.

key_changes_vs_lpddr4.change: CAS command moved before the read/write (WS_FS/WS_RD/WS_WR)
key_changes_vs_lpddr4.impact: The CAS command primarily synchronizes WCK to CK (it does not select a column), unlike LPDDR4's trailing CAS-2.
Bank-group timing (tCCD_L/tRRD_L) enables higher concurrency; 16n prefetch retained (NOT doubled).
Lower IO power; receiver DFE + (5B) tx/rx equalization required for SI.
On-the-wire single-bit error correction; reduced driven-bit count.

key_changes_vs_lpddr4.change: DVFS / DVFSC (VDD2H/VDD2L), deep sleep, Data-Copy / Write-X
key_changes_vs_lpddr4.impact: Fine-grained power scaling and data-transfer reduction for mobile battery life.
Low-power entry is a CA command bounded by CS, removing a pin and simplifying low-power control.

backward_compat_traps.rule: The internal WCK must be phase-locked to CK via a WCK2CK synchronization (WS_FS/WS_RD/WS_WR via CAS) before any high-speed read/write.
backward_compat_traps.trap: A controller that omits the WCK2CK sync (carry-over from a continuous-data-clock DDR mindset) will see undefined read/write data timing because WCK is otherwise disabled.

backward_compat_traps.rule: LPDDR5 has no CKE pin; low-power entry is a CA command that lasts until CS next goes high.
backward_compat_traps.trap: A controller expecting a CKE pin to gate the clock / enter power-down will not control LPDDR5 correctly.

backward_compat_traps.rule: In LPDDR5 the CAS command precedes the read/write and synchronizes WCK; it does NOT itself select a column.
backward_compat_traps.trap: Treating LPDDR5 CAS like LPDDR4's column-selecting CAS-2 produces wrong addressing/timing.

backward_compat_traps.rule: LPDDR4 column names C0-C9 are renamed in LPDDR5 to B0-B3 and C0-C5; writes must start at a multiple-of-16 address with B0-B3 zero; reads may request a non-zero B3.
backward_compat_traps.trap: Reusing LPDDR4 column-bit naming silently mis-addresses the burst start.

backward_compat_traps.rule: LPDDR5 VDDQ is 0.5 V (vs 0.6 V LPDDR4X, 1.5 V DDR3).
backward_compat_traps.trap: Driving LPDDR5 IO at a higher VDDQ damages the device.

backward_compat_traps.rule: Exiting Deep Sleep Mode requires the full initialization sequence (ZQ + WCK2CK + training).
backward_compat_traps.trap: Resuming traffic immediately after deep-sleep exit without re-init produces undefined behaviour.

fields.version_naming_history_note: LPDDR5 is the fifth generation of JEDEC's Low Power Double Data Rate SDRAM line, standardized by the JC-42.6 Low Power Memory committee as JESD209-5 (19 February 2019). The LPDDR generational naming convention is separate from the mainstream DDR family (the version numbers do not indicate that LPDDR5 and DDR5 share design, only that they share some technologies). JESD209-5B (2021) added the LPDDR5/5X speed extension (8533 Mbit/s), tx/rx equalization, and Adaptive Refresh Management; JESD209-5X covers the LPDDR5X branding. LPDDR5 distinguishes itself from DDR3 (JESD79-3) by its WCK on-demand clocking, JESD209-5 numbering, mobile low-voltage operation (VDDQ=0.5 V), and CA-bus command encoding rather than separate RAS/CAS/WE pins.
